ayahs.1: When the sun is wrapped up,
ayahs.2: These opening letters—known as the muqatta'at—are among the signs whose full meaning Allah kept with Himself. They open the surah by reminding the reader that this Book is from beyond human authorship: approach it with humility, not arrogance.
ayahs.5: when wild beasts are herded together,
ayahs.7: when souls are paired again with their bodies,
ayahs.8: when baby girls buried alive are asked
ayahs.9: for what crime they were killed,
ayahs.10: when records of deeds are laid open,
ayahs.11: when the sky is stripped away,
ayahs.12: when Hell is fiercely flared up,
ayahs.14: each soul will know what it brought along.
ayahs.15: I swear by the retreating stars
ayahs.17: by the night as it falls,
ayahs.18: and the day as it breaks—
ayahs.19: this Qur'an is the word of a noble messenger-angel,
ayahs.20: full of power, honoured by the Lord of the Throne,
ayahs.23: He saw that angel on the clear horizon,
ayahs.24: and he does not withhold what is revealed of the unseen.
ayahs.25: This is not the word of an outcast devil.
ayahs.26: So what other path would you take?
ayahs.27: This is only a Reminder for all the worlds—
ayahs.28: for whoever among you wills to walk the Sirat al-Mustaqim—the Straight Path.
ayahs.29: But you cannot will that except by the will of Allah, Rabb of all that exists.
